title: Tearful Scaloni Doubts Argentina Future as Messi Faces Final World Cup Curtain
excerpt: Argentina's head coach broke down at his post-match press conference after Spain's 1-0 extra-time World Cup final victory, while Messi's international career appears over at 39.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Lionel Scaloni left the press conference in tears, questioning his future after the final loss.
  • Messi, at 39, likely played his last World Cup match, scoring eight goals in the tournament.
  • Enzo Fernández's red card reduced Argentina to 10 men, leading to Spain's winning goal in extra time.
  • Goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez set a record with 11 saves in the final despite a broken finger.
  • Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni left his post-match press conference in tears after Spain's 1-0 extra-time victory, saying he needs to "think things over" before deciding his future.
  • Messi, who turned 39 during the tournament, almost certainly played his final World Cup match after scoring eight goals and four assists — but going scoreless in the final.
  • Enzo Fernández's second yellow card left Argentina down to 10 men for extra time, where Ferran Torres scored the winner in the 106th minute.
  • Goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez made a World Cup final-record 11 saves despite a broken finger, but could not deny Spain their second title.

A Coach Overcome

Lionel Scaloni sat before the assembled media at MetLife Stadium on Sunday night and tried to hold himself together. He could not.

Moments after Spain ended Argentina's bid to become the first team to defend the World Cup since Brazil in 1962, the 48-year-old broke down, cast doubt on his future, and walked out of his press conference to applause.

"I will talk to the president. I will fulfill my contract and then see. I feel the need to think things over because I don't know if it's possible to achieve something this great ever again."

— Lionel Scaloni, Argentina head coach

Scaloni, whose contract expires in December, did not explicitly resign. But what followed carried the tone of a farewell. "To keep going requires resetting yourself completely, building a group like this all over again — which will be hard to ever replicate," he said, his voice cracking. "And it hurts me to my very soul." He stood, wiped his face, and left the room.

> **"Of the 2022 title, he joked: "I already completed the game."**

Spain's Disciplined Masterclass

The final was never really a contest. Spain controlled 68% of possession before 80,663 at MetLife Stadium and outshot Argentina 20-0. Argentina did not register a single shot on target across 120 minutes.

The match turned in stoppage time when Enzo Fernández received a second yellow card — the first for dissent, the second for a reckless challenge on Pau Cubarsí. Down to 10 men, Argentina's task became near-impossible.

Spain needed 39 seconds of the second extra-time period to break through. Nico Williams headed Pedro Porro's cross back across goal for Ferran Torres to hammer a half-volley into the roof of the net from 10 yards. Goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez, playing through a broken finger, had produced a record 11 saves to keep the match scoreless until then.

Lionel Messi stood on the MetLife turf as confetti fell for Spain, hands behind his back, captain's armband still on his left biceps. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner wept as FIFA president Gianni Infantino draped a silver medal over his neck.

Messi, 39, has not officially announced his international retirement. But he hinted before the tournament that this was his last World Cup. Of the 2022 title, he joked: "I already completed the game. The game is over. I'm done." He will be 43 when the 2030 World Cup begins. No outfield player over 42 has ever appeared at the tournament.

The ending is cruel given the brilliance that preceded it. Messi opened with a hat trick against Algeria, scored a stunning equaliser against Egypt in the round of 16, and delivered two assists in the semifinal win over England. He finished with eight goals and four assists — narrowly missing the Golden Boot to Kylian Mbappé's 10. In the final, Spain's defence rendered him invisible.

"It's crystal clear to me that he will play up until he decides not to. He's the best football player ever to step foot on a pitch. What he did this World Cup is incredible."

— Lionel Scaloni on Messi

What Comes Next

Eight players started both the 2022 and 2026 finals. With a squad averaging nearly 29, significant turnover is inevitable. Young holdovers Valentín Barco, Nico Paz (both 21), and Giuliano Simeone (23) will carry the next generation.

Scaloni took over as interim coach in 2018 and won two Copa América titles and a World Cup. His post-match comments suggest he has already decided to step away. If he does, his successor inherits a squad in transition — but one built on a winning culture he spent eight years constructing.

Messi still has years on his Inter Miami contract; his club career will continue. But for the national team, Sunday at MetLife — the same ground where he tearfully retired after the 2016 Copa América, only to reverse course — may have been the final chapter. This time, there may be no coming back.
